caption: AI checks feel thorough but miss errors. This carousel shows a practical, no-fluff workflow to audit AI drafts. Save this as a reusable QA routine. Do you have a go-to step for verifying AI outputs? #AIQA #Productivity #Founders #BusinessDecisions

slides.title: Don't trust AI to verify
slides.body: Problem: AI outputs seem right but can be wrong. I'll give five prompts to audit them.

slides.title: 1. Diagnose quality
slides.body: Review [DOCUMENT]; list factual errors, contradictions, and omissions. Output: bullet list with issue, severity, suggested fix.

slides.title: 2. Improve clarity
slides.body: Rewrite [DOCUMENT] to fix factual errors, simplify sentences, add citations in [STYLE]. Output: revised document.

slides.title: 3. Apply to formats
slides.body: Create two deliverables from [DOCUMENT]: a 1-page executive summary and a client email. Output: both in bullets.

slides.title: 4. Check for bias
slides.body: Scan [DOCUMENT] for bias, assumptions, and unsupported claims. Output: list of flagged items with rationale.

slides.title: 5. Build QA workflow
slides.body: Create a reusable QA checklist for future AI work in [TEAM]. Output: ready-to-use checklist.

slides.title: Takeaway
slides.body: Final takeaway: with a structured QA, you catch errors early and ship reliable AI outputs.
